designDecisions.decision: Two-tier write: Tier 1 writes value cells from already-staged cad_property (all 6 counties, join on (county_fips, prop_id) -- no new acquire script needed for this tier). Tier 2 is a Williamson-only override: acquire-wcad-owner.mjs stages WCAD's own structured Owner dataset (bbia-wsxs) by direct quickrefid join (verified quickrefid IS the same key already used for Williamson CAD rows -- no crosswalk step needed, unlike the WCAD ag-valuation propertyid check in wave 1), and parcel-owner.mjs prefers the Tier 2 value over Tier 1 wherever both exist, citing the more authoritative source.

Add electric as a third fully independent sub-type on the same rail/job (parcel-utility-service.mjs), following the exact per-type independence pattern shipped in wave 1's hotfix PR #84 (own try/catch, own DELETE ... WHERE source=$1 AND utility_type=$2) -- a failed electric fetch/write must never risk previously-good water/sewer rows, and vice versa. tx_puct_ccn.utility_type CHECK constraint widened via idempotent ALTER TABLE to admit 'electric'.

Extend acquire-ag-valuation.mjs / parcel-ag-valuation.mjs to accept --county=48453 (Travis) alongside the existing --county=48491 (Williamson) refusal-gated switch, sourcing from TCAD's own structured ag-valuation dataset (confirmed same shape as WCAD's, not a crosswalk-needed case). tx_wcad_ag_valuation gains an additive county_fips column with a one-time backfill of existing Williamson rows to 48491 (name kept for git-blame continuity rather than renamed to a generic tx_ag_valuation -- a judgment call, not dictated by the dispatch).

New rail, Austin-only (TRAVIS_FIPS = 48453 scope-only refuse for any other county). Two new acquire scripts (acquire-austin-watershed.mjs, acquire-edwards-recharge-zone.mjs) stage Austin's own watershed-classification layer and the Edwards Aquifer recharge-zone layer separately; parcel-max-impervious-cover.mjs joins both via parcel centroid and resolves the LDC Ch. 25-8 crosswalk (IMPERVIOUS_COVER_CROSSWALK, hand-built from the ordinance text, cited section by section). Crosswalk is deliberately partial and honest: only 'WATER SUPPLY SUBURBAN' resolves to a percentage (30%, citing Sec. 25-8-423(B)) -- BSZ/SUBURBAN/URBAN/WATER SUPPLY RURAL are left unresolved with real cited reasons (the ordinance's own percentage for those depends on additional site-specific conditions this rail's inputs can't determine) rather than guessing a number. Unresolved watershed types produce no cell (left unaccounted), not a fabricated value.

All new write jobs added to src/control/writer-allowlist.mjs with liveRest:false, planRow:'F-01', edited personally (not delegated to subagents) to avoid multi-agent merge conflicts on this shared file -- same discipline as wave 1. cloudbuild.parcel-wave2.yaml authored personally, defining 5 new Cloud Run job definitions with an explicit deployment-order comment documenting the Williamson tx_wcad_ag_valuation county_fips backfill must complete before the Travis acquire step runs (both write into the same table).

openVerificationItemsAtCP1: WCAD Owner dataset quickrefid vs cad_property's existing Williamson key -- verified matching directly before writing the join (no crosswalk needed), mirroring the same discipline used for WCAD ag-valuation's propertyid check in wave 1.

TCAD ag-valuation dataset shape vs WCAD's -- verified same shape (both structured CAD exports with a per-parcel ag-use code and per-parcel acreage/value fields) before assuming the existing write job's SQL could extend cleanly with only a county_fips branch.
